chunks: Ali ibn Muhammad, raising it (mursal), from Shu'ayb al-'Aqarqufi, from Abu Baseer, who said:

I was seated before Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) when a questioner asked him, saying: 'May I be your ransom, O son of the Messenger of God! From where did misery befall the people of disobedience such that God decreed for them in His knowledge punishment for their deeds?'

So Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'O questioner! The decree of God, Mighty and Majestic, is such that none of His creation can fulfill it as it deserves. So when He decreed that, He bestowed upon the people of His love the strength to recognize Him, and lifted from them the burden of deeds according to the reality of what they are deserving of.'

And He bestowed upon the people of disobedience the strength for their disobedience — due to the precedence of His knowledge regarding them — and He prevented them from the capacity to accept from Him. So they conformed to what had preceded for them in His knowledge, and they were unable to attain a state that would save them from His punishment — because His knowledge is more deserving of the reality of ratification. And this is the meaning of: He willed what He willed — and it is His secret.

key_terms.إطاقة القبول: The capacity for acceptance — the ability to receive and respond to divine guidance; those in disobedience are described as being denied this
key_terms.الشقاء: Misery/wretchedness (shaqa') — the condition of those who are spiritually lost and destined for punishment, as opposed to happiness (sa'adah)
key_terms.القوة على المعصية: The strength for disobedience — God granting the physical/volitional capacity to those already known in His knowledge to disobey
key_terms.حكم الله: The decree/judgment of God — here referring to God's eternal predetermination, which no creature can fully stand up to in its proper right
key_terms.سره: His secret — the divine mystery of will and foreknowledge that transcends human rational categories

ai.seo_question: Why does God punish sinners if He already knew they would sin? What does Imam al-Sadiq say about divine foreknowledge and human disobedience?
ai.summary: In this hadith, Abu Baseer recounts sitting before Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) when a questioner raised the profound theological problem: if God's prior knowledge already determined the fate of sinners, how can their punishment be just? The Imam responded by explaining that God's decree is beyond the capacity of any creature to fully grasp. He clarified that God bestows strength for good upon those who love Him, and correspondingly permits those who were always destined for disobedience (in God's eternal knowledge) to follow that path — since it is His eternal knowledge itself that is the final arbiter. The Imam resolves the tension between divine foreknowledge and human accountability by pointing to the inscrutable divine will ('He willed what He willed'), affirming that this mystery is a divine secret beyond full human comprehension.
